_notes.interface_version_drift_warning: Three local copies of ICasinoGameV2.sol disagree: chain-contracts-main (protocol repo, == casino-sdk/contracts) has a `uint8 outcome` field on StepResult but NO quoteRiskParams and NO quoteForfeitPayout; the SDK docs bundle adds quoteRiskParams but still has no quoteForfeitPayout; happydaze (a real shipped integration) drops the `outcome` field but has BOTH quoteRiskParams and quoteForfeitPayout. rubric/ICasinoGameV2.sol uses happydaze's version (the superset / most-current-looking) as the reference for interface checks. This needs a definitive answer from whoever owns the protocol repo before this pipeline is trusted for real submissions -- see README 'Open questions'.

rules.description: Contract(s) compile cleanly under solc ^0.8.30 via forge build.
Contract implements all required ICasinoGameV2 functions with matching selectors (per rubric/ICasinoGameV2.sol).
quoteCaps, quoteRiskParams, onSessionStart, onPlayerAction, onRandomness, quoteForfeitPayout are all declared view or pure (no state mutation) -- checked via ABI stateMutability.
No selfdestruct usage.
No delegatecall usage.
No tx.origin usage (phishing/auth bypass vector).
Low-level value-call patterns (.call{value:) flagged for manual/AI review.
block.timestamp / blockhash / block.prevrandao / block.difficulty not used as a randomness source -- randomness must come only from the onRandomness callback parameter.
Inline assembly blocks flagged for manual/AI review.
forge lint (high/medium severity) findings surfaced directly.
No use of a stale `probabilityBps` field name -- the live interface uses `probabilityWad`.
game.manifest.json exists at the guest's own origin/root.
schemaVersion == 1.
gameId is a non-empty string.
apiVersion == 1.
defaultLocale is non-empty and present in locales with a non-empty name.
presentation.mode is 'full-iframe' or 'embedded'.
presentation.minHeight is a finite number.
presentation.hostPanels.{openSession,history,status} are booleans.
capabilities.{openSession,submitAction,forfeitExpiredSession,cancelStuckRandomness,resize} are all booleans present, and capabilities.openSession === true for a betting game.
gameId's canonical form (strip trailing 'Game', lowercase, strip non-alphanumerics) is plausible given the contract name -- informational, real check happens at whitelist/registration time.

Guest code never signs or broadcasts a transaction and never connects a wallet directly (no ethers.Wallet/signTransaction/sendTransaction/window.ethereum.request signing calls) -- it must only call hostApi.openSession/submitAction/cancelStuckRandomness.
postMessage/Penpal allowedOrigins does not silently resolve to '*' in a way that looks production-bound (dev-only per VISUAL_AND_UX.md).
Guest code visibly uses the SDK bridge pattern (connectGameToHost / Penpal WindowMessenger) rather than a custom/ad-hoc protocol.
npm audit high/critical advisories in guest dependencies.
ESLint / tsc pass, if a config is present (best-effort, non-blocking if absent).
gameData is decoded identically (same paytable/variant) across quoteCaps, quoteRiskParams, and onSessionStart/onRandomness.
onPlayerAction correctly reverts for instant/single-step games with no legitimate mid-round action, or correctly validates/handles actions for multi-step games.
The actual payout produced by onRandomness/onPlayerAction can never exceed the maxPayout quoted by quoteRiskParams for the same wager/gameData, across every reachable code path.
probabilityWad is the probability of the top-tier/jackpot outcome specifically (not 'any win' or an average), is <= 1e18, and is internally consistent with the contract's own odds table.
expectedPayout matches the RTP actually implied by the paytable/weights used in onRandomness (no drift between quoted and simulated RTP).
Session phase-machine transitions (nextPhase / requestRandomnessNow) are correct for the game's step pattern and cannot be driven into an invalid or permanently stuck state.
onSessionStart is deterministic and side-effect-free enough to be safely called twice (once as a sessionId==0 simulation, per CONTRACT_CONSTRAINTS.md).

UI never independently computes or lets the player submit a payout figure that isn't sourced from host-pushed on-chain state (gameState/balances are hints only; facet + game contract are authoritative).
General security review: reentrancy-shaped external calls, backdoors/owner bypass, hardcoded addresses or credentials, obfuscated or suspicious logic not caught by the static grep rules.
UI-contract integration correctness: guest's hostApi.openSession/submitAction gameData encoding matches what the contract actually decodes; sessionKey correlation is handled correctly.
manifest capabilities truthfully reflect the contract's actual shape (e.g. submitAction:false for a contract whose onPlayerAction always reverts).

Narrative risk-engine compliance: if maxPayout/wager exceeds ~100x and probabilityWad is under ~0.1%, the game is heavy-tail and should be flagged as such for the tiered jackpot-reserve path rather than naive VaR.
